name: ECU Diagnostics & Firmware Security
description: Security assessment of electronic control unit diagnostic services and firmware. Covers UDS (ISO 14229), OBD-II legislated modes (ISO 15031, SAE J1979), KWP2000 and DoIP (ISO 13400) diagnostics; diagnostic session and SecurityAccess (service 0x27) seed-key analysis, authenticated diagnostics (service 0x29), memory read and write services, and routine control abuse; flash bootloader and reprogramming assessment (RequestDownload, TransferData), signed firmware verification, rollback and anti-downgrade protection, and calibration access over XCP. Also covers extraction and analysis of ECU firmware images and their AUTOSAR configuration. The buses that carry these diagnostic services belong to ICSIOT-AUTO-IVN; chip-level and debug-port firmware extraction belongs to HWSEC-EMBED-FW and HWSEC-EMBED-DBG; generic binary analysis belongs to SWSEC-RE-DISASM.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to ECU diagnostics or automotive firmware security

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands how ECUs are diagnosed and reprogrammed, and why those paths are an attack surface
evidence: Can explain the UDS request/response model, diagnostic sessions and negative response codes
Distinguishes legislated OBD-II modes from manufacturer-specific UDS services
Understands that SecurityAccess seed-key exchange is an authentication step and why weak seeds matter
Can describe the flash reprogramming sequence at a conceptual level

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Enumerates and exercises diagnostic services on a bench ECU under supervision
evidence: Scans for responding diagnostic addresses and supported services with tooling such as caringcaribou or custom scripts
Requests DTCs, data identifiers and ECU identification under guidance
Transitions diagnostic sessions and documents which services each session unlocks
Extracts a firmware image from a bench ECU using a documented procedure under supervision
Keeps guided activity to read-only diagnostic services, escalating any write, routine-control or reprogramming request to the supervising assessor

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently assesses an ECU's diagnostic interface and firmware against a defined scope
evidence: Enumerates the full diagnostic service and DID/RID surface and identifies services reachable without authentication
Analyses SecurityAccess implementations for weak or static seeds, short key spaces, missing delay and attempt counters, and brute-forces them where scope permits
Assesses whether safety-relevant routines or memory write services are reachable outside a protected session or while the vehicle is in motion
Reviews the flash bootloader for signature verification, version anti-rollback and failure handling
Analyses an extracted firmware image for hardcoded secrets, diagnostic backdoors and weak cryptographic material

Plans testing so that memory-write, routine-control and flash reprogramming services are exercised only on bench ECUs or immobilised vehicles with a documented recovery path, and so that SecurityAccess brute force respects attempt counters and lockout behaviour
Produces findings that state preconditions and real-world reachability for each diagnostic weakness

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Assesses complex and protected diagnostic implementations; mentors others
evidence: Reverse engineers proprietary seed-key algorithms out of firmware or tester software and demonstrates key derivation
Evaluates authenticated diagnostics (service 0x29) and certificate-based tester authentication, including trust anchor and revocation handling
Assesses secure flashing end to end: key provisioning, signature scheme, chain of trust and downgrade resistance
Builds custom UDS and DoIP tooling or fuzzers for manufacturer-specific service sets
Chains diagnostic findings with in-vehicle network or connectivity findings into end-to-end attack paths
Mentors staff on diagnostic assessment methodology and safe bench and vehicle practice

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines the lab's ECU diagnostic and firmware assessment methodology; recognised authority
evidence: Authored the lab's ECU diagnostics and firmware assessment methodology and its safe reprogramming rules
Published research or disclosed vulnerabilities in diagnostic implementations, seed-key schemes or flash bootloaders
Advises manufacturers or suppliers on diagnostic hardening and secure update design
Contributes to automotive diagnostic or cybersecurity standards and industry working groups

assessment_methods.description: On a bench ECU, enumerate the supported diagnostic services, identify which are reachable without SecurityAccess, defeat or assess the seed-key scheme, and judge whether the flash bootloader accepts unsigned or downgraded firmware
Given an extracted ECU firmware image and a diagnostic specification, locate the seed-key routine and determine whether the key can be derived offline
Review an ECU diagnostic assessment report for service coverage, correctness of claimed preconditions, and accuracy of reachability and impact statements

equipment: UDS-capable vehicle communication interface (e.g. VN1600-class or equivalent)
Bench ECU with flash programming harness
Regulated bench power supply with current monitoring
